figures.shows: the three entangler blocks, each repeated D times on qubits q0 to qN (initial state |1> on the lowest qubits, |0> on the others): (a) a staircase of U1,ex exchange gates between neighbouring qubits; (b) a column of Rz rotations on every qubit followed by a staircase of U2,ex gates; (c) a column of general rotations R on every qubit followed by one all-to-all CNOT block U_CNOT.

figures.shows: H2 dissociation with UCCSD and active spaces AS 4, AS 6 and AS 8. Upper panel: energy E in Ha (y, about -1.15 to -0.90) against bond distance in Angstrom (x, about 0.5 to 2.2); HF curve (red) rises above the others, the analytic p/h solution is the black curve, AS 4 orange, AS 6 green, AS 8 blue. Lower panel: E - Eexact in mHa (y, 0 to about 20) with a shaded chemical-accuracy band near the bottom; the AS 4 errors are the highest, the AS 8 errors lie on the band at about 0 mHa.
figures.confirmed_by: Fig. 3 shows the dissociation proﬁle for the H2 molecule computed using VQE approach and the UCCSD Ansatz with diﬀerent sizes of the active space (AS)

figures.shows: H2O dissociation with UCCSD and active spaces AS 8, AS 10 and AS 12. Upper panel: energy E in Ha (y, about -16.95 to -16.65) against bond distance in Angstrom (x, about 0.7 to 2.8); HF red curve rises above the rest, black analytic p/h curve, AS 8 orange, AS 10 green, AS 12 blue. Lower panel: E - Eexact in mHa (y, 0 to about 20) with the chemical-accuracy band; the AS 8 errors peak at about 19 mHa near 1.3 Angstrom, AS 10 stays lower, AS 12 stays near the band. An inset marks the orbitals included in each active space.
figures.confirmed_by: Fig. 4 reports the same energy proﬁles for the asymmetric stretch of a O-H bond of a water molecule.

figures.shows: Trotter error in Ha (y, logarithmic, from 10^-13 to 10^-7) against the number of Trotter steps (x, 0 to 100) for H2 at a bond length of 0.592 Angstrom. Green circles (analytic dependence, Eq. 26) fall from about 3e-8 at n = 1 to about 3e-12 at n = 100. Red triangles (VQE reoptimization at each n, Eq. 27) stay at about 2e-13 at n = 1 and fall slowly to about 4e-14 at n = 100.
figures.confirmed_by: In Fig. 5, we summarize the results for the Trotter approximation in the Hydrogen molecule.

figures.shows: H2 dissociation using the p/h Hamiltonian and the heuristic Ansatz with D = 8 blocks. Lower panel: E - Eexact in mHa (y, 0 to about 33) with the chemical-accuracy band; entanglers 1 and 2 lie near 0 to about 10 mHa, entangler 3 reaches about 33 mHa around 1.1 to 1.3 Angstrom.

papers.what_it_is: An IBM Research paper that proposes a particle-hole Hamiltonian, a single-Trotter-step q-UCCSD circuit and particle-conserving exchange-gate entanglers for VQE ground-state energies, simulated on H2 and H2O.

assertions.value: The authors define an equivalent electronic structure Hamiltonian in the particle-hole (p/h) picture that has the Hartree-Fock state as its reference (vacuum) state.
quotes: we deﬁne an equivalent electronic structure Hamiltonian in
the particle-hole (p/h) picture that has |Φ0 as reference (vacuum) state.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the p/h Hamiltonian in Section II.A.

assertions.value: The authors define a new vacuum state in the N-particle sector of the Fock space, built by creating the N occupied orbitals, which coincides with the Slater determinant solution of the HF problem with N electrons.
quotes: which coincides with the Slater determinant solution of the HF problem with N electrons.
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition of the reference state in Section II.A.

assertions.value: The authors call the holes and particles generated by excitation operators relative to the HF ground state quasi-particles.
quotes: ground state |Φ0 are called quasi-particles.
assertions.certainty_reason: A definition the paper gives.

assertions.value: The authors choose to apply the p/h transformation to the Hamiltonian, not to the wavefunction, because in VQE the Hamiltonian is a measured quantity while the wavefunction is encoded in the qubit register.
quotes: For practical convenience, we chose the second approach as in the VQE algorithm the Hamiltonian is a measured quantity while the wavefunction is encoded in the qubit register
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own design choice.

assertions.value: The authors state that the difference between the UCC and variational-CC energies is in general very small, citing another work.
quotes: However, the difference between the UCC and variational-CC energies is in general very small [47].
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to cited work.

assertions.value: The authors restrict their UCC implementation to the UCCSD case (single and double excitations), and state that going to higher excitations needs longer circuits that are at present unpractical from experimental as well as simulation perspectives.
quotes: In the following, we will restrict our implementation to the UCCSD case

the extension to higher excitations does not imply any further development but only requires the implementation of longer circuits that are at present unpractical from experimental, as well as simulation perspectives.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and limit.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that within the p/h formalism it is possible to design valid quantum algorithms for electronic structure problems in near-term quantum computers with a favourable scaling in terms of parameters and gate counts.
quotes: In conclusion, we show that within the p/h-formalism it is possible to design valid quantum algorithms for the solution of electronic structure problems in near-term quantum computers with a favourable scaling in terms of parameters and gate counts.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author conclusion; the paper reports no hardware run and no scaling study.
assertions.reader_inference: Only H2 and H2O are simulated; no scaling with system size is measured.

assertions.value: The authors state that CCSD(T), with a scaling of O(N 7) (N to the seventh power), is often considered the gold standard for quantum chemistry calculations, and that CC truncated at fourth order (CCSDTQ) scales as O(N 10) (N to the tenth power).
quotes: with a scaling O(N 7) is often considered the
O(N 10) for the CC approach when the expansion is truncated at the fourth order
assertions.certainty_reason: Background attributed to cited works.

assertions.value: The authors state that CCSD(T) energies have an error within chemical accuracy, errors less than 1 - 5 kcal/mol = 0.043 - 0.22 eV, for many systems, when no strong static correlation or multi-reference character of the ground state is present.
quotes: errors less than 1 - 5 kcal/mol = 0.043 - 0.22 eV
when no strong static correlation or multi-reference character of the ground state is present
assertions.certainty_reason: Background attributed to cited works.

assertions.value: The authors state that the classically inspired approach has the drawback that the number of parameters (gate angles) increases significantly with the number of electrons, which limits scaling to larger systems.
quotes: the number of parameters (gate angles) increases signiﬁcantly with the number of electrons
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim without a measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that second quantization avoids the costly discretization of physical space needed in first quantization, and that first quantization methods will require a larger number of qubits even for small systems such as H2.
quotes: This avoids the costly discretization of the physical space needed in the ﬁrst quantization (FQ) picture.
while methods in FQ will require a larger number of qubits even for the simulation of small systems such as H2.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim without a count.

assertions.value: The authors state in Appendix A that, with the assignment A = sigma_y,j sigma_x,i and B = minus sigma_x,j sigma_y,i, the commutators [A,[A,B]], [B,[A,B]] and [A,B] vanish, so that the exponential of the sum equals the product of exponentials exactly.
quotes: all commutators [Aˆ, [Aˆ, Bˆ]], [Bˆ, [Aˆ, Bˆ]] and [Aˆ, Bˆ] vanish.
assertions.certainty_reason: The statement is made without a displayed calculation, and the exact-splitting conclusion is only partly quoted.
assertions.reader_inference: The sentence reads Glauber's formula then simplifies exactly to e^(A+B) = e^A e^B.

assertions.value: The authors state in Appendix A that they apply the Trotter approximation to first order to the UCCSD operator, and apply the Trotter expansion to first order once more before the Jordan-Wigner transformation.
quotes: Applying once more the Trotter expansion to ﬁrst order we get
assertions.certainty_reason: A derivation step the paper shows without error analysis.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 3: for H2 with UCCSD, the E - Eexact error of the smallest active space (orange) is about 18 mHa to about 19 mHa at short bond lengths and falls to about 13 mHa near about 2 Angstrom, the middle active space (green) lies at about 11 mHa to about 15 mHa, and the largest (blue) lies at about 0 mHa, within the chemical accuracy band.
quotes: Lower panel: Corresponding energy errors along the dissociation proﬁle.
The blue shaded area corresponds to the energy range within chemical accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Values read by eye from a plot.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says AS4 runs approximately in parallel to the exact curve; the plot shows an error of about 13 to 19 mHa, well outside the chemical-accuracy band.
